reviews.body:
Thanks for fixing Responses API `instructions` and `max_output_tokens` capture (and closing the `privacyMode` leak of `instructions` via `$ai_model_parameters`!). The core mapping works cleanly across both scalar and array `input` payloads and verified against `sdk-mock-server` with `OpenAI` 2.14.0.

Left two inline concerns before approval:
1. `instructions` are silently dropped when `input` is omitted/`null` (e.g., `previous_response_id`/`conversation` continuations) or when paired with a Responses stored `prompt` object.
2. The `JsonArray` `input` (`DeepClone()`) branch and `privacyMode: true` behavior lack unit test coverage.

AI-assisted review.

Thanks for the quick follow-up! Both earlier concerns (capturing `instructions` when `input` is omitted/`null` or alongside a stored `prompt` object, plus adding `JsonArray` `DeepClone` and `privacyMode: true` coverage) are cleanly addressed.

Verified locally with multi-TFM Release builds (`netstandard2.1` + `net8.0`), 40/40 `PostHog.AI.Tests`, `dotnet format`, and both synthetic and live OpenAI (`gpt-6-luna`) Responses API completions captured via `sdk-mock-server` with `OpenAI` 2.14.0.

AI-assisted review.

comments.body:
Thanks, good catch. `instructions` is now read before the legacy `prompt` fallback and added as a leading system message whether `input` is absent, `null`, a string or an array, and also when a stored `prompt` object is present (legacy completions never send `instructions`, so their `prompt` capture is unchanged). Added tests for the `previous_response_id` cases (input omitted / null) and for stored prompt + array input; they fail on the previous head and pass now (`PostHogOpenAIHandlerTests`). Also added `SendAsyncOmitsResponsesInstructionsWhenPrivacyModeIsTrue` (inside `PostHogAIContext.BeginScope(privacyMode: true)` with `instructions` set, neither `$ai_input` nor `$ai_model_parameters` contains the instructions text). The array input / `DeepClone` case is covered by `SendAsyncCapturesResponsesInstructionsWithStoredPromptAndArrayInput`. 35/35 now.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
